title: Late-binding scratch scheduler and KV-window coalescing to reduce GPU workspace
author: Elena Martinez
release_notes: Introduce late-binding scratch scheduler and KV-window coalescing. Typical GPU working set reduction 12-28% across validated models; no API changes. Rollout behind runtime flag with canary on Dedicated clusters.
description:
Context and motivation: production workloads show fragmented scratch allocation during mixed-sequence traffic and inflated KV cache live ranges due to conservative pre-binding of scratch buffers and eager KV segment retention. This PR implements a late-binding scratch scheduler that defers physical allocation until kernel dispatch time and a complementary KV-window coalescer that merges adjacent short-lived KV segments into temporally contiguous windows. Together these reduce transient workspace and activation residency across the serving runtime without changing model shards or checkpoint formats.

What I changed (summary): implemented a scheduler pass that records logical buffer lifetimes and performs placement at enqueue->dispatch boundary; added a compacting policy that attempts to co-allocate small scratch requests into a single contiguous slab when they are non-overlapping at dispatch. Implemented KV-window coalescing which tracks short-lived KV writes (typically cache of recent prefixes/tokens) and merges windows within a configurable delta to reduce number of active KV allocations. Added a runtime flag runtime.scratch.late_binding_enabled (default: false) and runtime.kv.coalesce_window_ms (default: 50ms) to make rollout gradual.

Design details: the late-binding scheduler keeps a small shadow lifetimes map in the dispatcher (lightweight metadata) and defers mapping to device addresses until the kernel is about to run. This avoids long-lived reservations for speculative scratch during batching expansion. When coallocation is possible the scheduler issues a single allocation and partitions it with offset descriptors; partitions are pinned only for the kernel duration. The KV-window coalescer uses a sliding-window heuristic and a low-overhead sampler to avoid global locking; it merges writes that are within the delta and have compatible alignment constraints.

Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for lifetime inference and coalesce correctness; integration tests in the runtime CI harness exercising continuous batching scenarios (variable sequence length mix). Microbenchmarks across our standard model set (gpt-small, gpt-medium, llama-7b, open-llama-13b) show GPU resident memory reductions ranging from 12% (gpt-small) to 28% (llama-7b) at p50 working set, measured under 75th-percentile request concurrency profile. Tail (p99) latency improved by ~8-12ms for long prompts due to reduced activation spill. End-to-end throughput shows negligible regression (<2%) for latency-sensitive configs and slight throughput gain (1-4%) in batch-friendly configs.

Compatibility and safety: no model or checkpoint format changes. The changes are guarded by runtime flags and a canary rollout plan; we added health-probes and fallback that revert to pre-binding on allocation contention or unexpected fragmentation. All new code paths have fuzzed allocation tests to prevent OOB.

Rollout plan: merge to main; enable feature flag for internal Dedicated canaries for 72h; if stable, enable for 10% of Hosted traffic for 24h with observability knobs (scratch_alloc_ratio, kv_active_windows, eviction_rate). Full enable after 1 week depending on metrics.

Related work: builds on earlier activation packing and checkpoint trimming work (ENG-1164, internal notes on arena tuning). Differentiator: this approach avoids heavy arena reorganization by deferring binding and targeting short-lived KV churn.
